pages.text: The $(thing)Molten Salt Reactor$() runs on $(thing)liquid fuel$(). Instead of arranging heat sinks and moderators, you pump $(thing)carrier salt$() through a chamber packed with $(thing)fuel pebbles$() and manage two coupled stats - $(thing)temperature$() and $(thing)reactivity$().

It does $(o)not$() make power directly. It turns $(thing)cold salt$() into $(thing)hot salt$(); pump that hot salt to a $(l:heat_exchanger/general)Heat Exchanger$() and on to a Turbine. Pumping hot salt out is also the core's $(o)only cooling$() - stop, and it overheats.

Place exactly one $(thing)Controller$() in the shell to form the reactor. It runs the simulation and owns the salt tanks and pebble slots. Its GUI reports temperature, reactivity, depletion and the salt rates.

The MSR reuses the fission shell. Edges and corners are $(thing)Reactor Casing$(); walls can be Casing, $(thing)Reactor Glass$(), or both. The shell is a cube from $(thing)5x5x5$() up to $(thing)26x26x26$().

Fill the $(o)entire interior$() with $(thing)MSR Fuel Cells$() - no other interior block is allowed. The fuel-cell count sets the reactor's salt volume and heat budget, so a bigger core holds more and runs harder.

$(thing)Ports$() move everything in and out: $(item)cold salt$() in, $(item)hot salt$() out, $(item)pebbles$() in, $(item)depleted pebbles$() out. One port type carries both items and fluid. A port also emits a comparator signal (Temperature or Depletion).

$(thing)Fuel$() is loaded as $(item)TRISO pebbles$() - the $(thing)_tr$() fuel variants, e.g. Thorium, LEU-235, HEU-235, Plutonium. As a pebble burns out it leaves a $(thing)depleted pebble$() in the output slot. $(thing)Carrier salt$() is $(item)FLiBe Molten Salt$(); the reactor pumps it in cold and out hot.
A 7x7x7 build: a casing-and-glass shell around a solid 5x5x5 core of Fuel Cells, with the Controller and an Irradiator on one wall and a pair of Ports on each side wall.

$(thing)Running it:$() pipe cold salt in, load pebbles, apply redstone. With enough fuel and salt the core goes $(thing)critical$() and heats up. Reactivity has a $(o)negative temperature coefficient$() - it falls as the core warms, so it self-stabilizes. Raise the $(thing)salt output rate$() to keep temperature off the 2000 K ceiling. The reactor can also be read and driven from $(thing)computers$() (type $(thing)nc_msr_reactor$()).
